paragraphs.text: Local Russian speech recognition (GigaAM-v3) for DeepSeek Harness voice input — offline, CPU, MIT
# dsh-speech-to-text-ru

**Local Russian speech recognition for DeepSeek Harness voice input.**
Adds a second, fully offline

recognizer — **GigaAM-v3 e2e CTC int8** — next to the shipped
SenseVoice provider, which understands

only Chinese, English, Cantonese, Japanese and Korean.
Audio never leaves the machine.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why

DSH's built-in **Voice input** plugin transcribes with SenseVoiceSmall, which has no Russian
support

. This bundle registers another `speechToText` provider backed by GigaAM-v3 (Sber's
Russian ASR foun

dation model, MIT) running on the `sherpa-onnx` native runtime that DSH already
ships. No cloud, no
API keys, no Python, no extra services.
## Highlights

| Model | GigaAM-v3 **e2e** CTC INT8 (punctuation, casing and number normalization included) |
| Qua
lity | **3.0 % WER** on the reference Russian set, **0 lexical errors** (only inverse text normaliza

tion differences) |
| Speed | **RTF 0.017** @ 2 threads — an 8.4 s phrase decodes in **~0.17 s**, mo

del load ~0.36 s |
| Memory | peak RSS **~564 MiB**; the worker is stopped after `idleTimeoutMs` |
|

Download | 319.9 MB model + 2 KB tokens + 1.8 MB Silero VAD, verified by size and SHA-256 |
| Langu

ages | `ru` (native), `auto`; multilingual Whisper fallback engine adds `en` and 99 more |
| Privacy

| CPU inference on the Host; audio never leaves the machine |
| Platforms | macOS arm64/x64, Linux
x64/arm64, Windows x64 (whatever DSH Desktop supports) |
## Requirements

- **DSH Desktop ≥ 0.2.1-rc.5** (or a CLI/Web profile composed from `dsh-base` + `dsh-web-app`).
- ~3

30 MB disk for the model cache and ~0.6 GB RAM while the recognizer is loaded.
- Network access for

the first model download (Hugging Face, with `hf-mirror.com` fallback).
Fully offline machines can p
re-seed the cache — see Offline install.
## Install

> **Order matters.** Enable the built-in **Voice input** first, then add this bundle. DSH applies
>

bundle patches in `dsh.profile.bundles` order, so the Russian bundle has to sit *after* the
> voice-

input bundle to make itself the default recognizer. The one-command installer below does
> this for

you; with the manual route, pick **GigaAM-v3 · RU (int8)** once in Settings if the order
> was the o

ther way round (DSH persists the selection), or append the small patch block that
> `scripts/install

nd (DSH persists the selection), or append the small patch block that
> `scripts/install.sh` writes.
### One command (recommended)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script uses the `dsh` CLI that ships with DSH Desktop, backs up the profile, enables **Voice
inp

ut**, installs/selects this bundle (`dsh plugin add`, so pnpm pulls the pinned
`sherpa-onnx-node@1.1

3.8` runtime for your platform) and pins `defaultProvider: gigaam-ru`,
`language: ru` in the profile
patch — so later toggling cannot change the default.
### Manual

1. In DSH open **Plugins** and switch **Voice input** on — that adds the microphone UI, the
`speechT

oText` service and its settings.
2. Add the bundle (the `dsh` CLI is
`/Applications/DeepSeek Harness

.app/Contents/Resources/runtime/cli/bin/dsh` on macOS; add it to
`PATH` or call it by full path):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

3. Refresh the app window (`Cmd+R` / `Ctrl+R`). Open **Settings → Voice input**: the recognizer
shou

ld be **GigaAM-v3 · RU (int8)** with language **ru**. If it is not (for example you enabled
Voice in
put after installing the bundle), select it once — DSH stores the choice per profile.
Other sources:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Distribution
The package is a normal DSH bundle, so it can be distributed in several ways:
| Source | Command |
| GitHub (recommended) | `dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:almaziphone/dsh-speech-to-text-ru`

|
| Release tarball | `dsh plugin --profile desktop add ./dsh-speech-to-text-ru-0.1.0.tgz` |
| npm

registry | `dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-speech-to-text-ru` |
| Local checkout | `dsh plugin
--profile desktop add /path/to/checkout` |

Model weights are **not** bundled: the published package is ~30 KB, while the pinned GigaAM-v3
INT8

weights (319.9 MB) and Silero VAD (1.8 MB) — ~322 MB together — are downloaded once on the
target ma

chine at first preparation and verified against the pinned SHA-256 hashes. Offline
machines can copy

`~/.dsh/speech-to-text/gigaam-ru/` instead, or use `scripts/install-from-checkout.sh`
on a clone.
Maintainers publish with:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## First use

The model is **not** bundled with the package. On first preparation DSH downloads the pinned
assets

from Hugging Face (revision pinned, size + SHA-256 verified while streaming) into
`~/.dsh/speech-to-

(revision pinned, size + SHA-256 verified while streaming) into
`~/.dsh/speech-to-text/gigaam-ru/`:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use **Download and prepare** in the voice settings, or just press the microphone: the provider
wakes
the worker and loads the model (≈0.4 s) once the cache is complete.
### Offline install

Copy the cache directory from a prepared machine to the same path on the target machine (the
provide

r re-verifies every file against the pinned SHA-256 before use), or point the provider at
existing f

iles through `modelDirectory` / `vadModelPath` in your profile patch. To forbid public
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- Assets are **revision-pinned** on Hugging Face with size + SHA-256 verification while
streaming; a

verified file is never downloaded again.
- The native `sherpa-onnx-node` runtime comes from the pac

kage dependency (or the copy inside the
DSH app bundle as a fallback) — this package never bundles p

latform binaries.
- The worker is a Node child process with a random 32-byte bearer token; the loopb

ack listener
only accepts `POST /transcribe` from the Host. Audio stays in memory.
- The provider is

a normal DSH plugin entry (`apply/inject`) with a preparation state machine
(`check → download → ve

rify → load`), so the standard voice UI cards, progress, cancellation and
settings work unchanged.
## Privacy

Model weights are downloaded from Hugging Face; nothing else touches the network. Recordings are
tra

nscribed on the Host CPU, in memory, by a local process, and are never uploaded. No API keys,
no tel
emetry from this plugin.
